title: Audit Skyline: operator contracts & fastpath playbook
body:
Summary:

This is a lightweight PRD-draft / playbook for a compact operator-oriented audit surface we are calling 'Audit Skyline'. Goal: enable fast, auditable handshakes for customer-managed VPC onboarding and emergency network changes with minimal evidence payloads and a small set of approval gates. Target customers: enterprise Private deployments with rigorous change controls but limited SIEM ingestion budgets.

Problem statement:
- Current onboarding/approval flows produce very large audit bundles that are costly to store and slow to review.
- Operators want a quick way to validate that a change is authorized and safe (canary/rollback paths) without pulling full packet captures or full-config diffs.
- Customers need cryptographic receipts or assertions to attach to their change tickets for compliance, but we must avoid leaking secret internal traces.

Design principles / constraints:
- Keep evidence minimal: canonicalize to a small set of fields that are sufficient for compliance reviews and automated triage.
- Human-reviewable: a one-page summary (Audit Skyline card) that answers who/what/when and provides links to deeper artifacts only when requested.
- Must support offline handoffs (air-gapped customers) via compact signed receipts.
- Fastpath mode: allow operators to approve low-risk changes with a single approver and a compact evidence set; higher-risk changes require multi-approver gating.
- Interoperable: provide templates that map to customer SIEM/AR (Splunk, Sumo, CrowdStrike) as simple key-value payloads.

Core components (high-level):
1) Audit Skyline Card (summary artifact)
   - One-line change description (50 chars)
   - Actor: user/service account (email or service:fqdn)
   - Action: change-type enum (ROUTE_UPDATE|FW_RULE|BGP_PEER|CERT_ROTATION)
   - Target resource id (short canonical id)
   - Risk score (low|med|high) computed by local heuristics
   - Approval chain: approver ids and approval method (UI|CLI|API)
   - Signed receipt id (compact signature token)
   - Link to deeper evidence (s3:// or local path or ephemeral URL)

2) Minimal Evidence Receipt (MER) template
   - MER.v0.3 fields (newline-separated KV for ease of ingestion):
     - receipt_id: <uuid>
     - receipt_version: 0.3
     - issuer: redwood-controlplane@redwood.com
     - subject: customer-account-id
     - change_type: BGP_PEER
     - actor: ops-team@example.com
     - timestamp: 2026-02-25T21:34:12Z
     - summary_hash: sha256:abcd... (hash of compact change summary)
     - signature: base64sig...
   - MER is intentionally small (~1-3KB) so it can be attached to Jira and pushed to customer ticketing systems.

3) Approval gate presets (fastpath / standard / locked)
   - Fastpath: single-person approval, risk must be low, no new CIDR blocks, no customer-data-plane outage impact. Auto-rollback window = 15m.
   - Standard: two independent approvers OR canary rollout + telemetry smoke check. Auto-rollback = 1h.
   - Locked: multi-signer (2 from different roles) + pre-signed MER + mandatory forensic bundle collection. Auto-rollback requires manual intervening.

Operator runbook (fastpath example):
- Pre-check (automated): run 'skyline preflight' which returns a compact risk score and MER draft.
- Approver reviews Audit Skyline card in Console (UI) or CLI shortcut.
- Approver runs smoke probe (automated health check; 3 probes: control-plane API ping, telemetry delta, customer connectivity check).
- If probes pass and risk=low -> Approve fastpath. System emits MER and Audit Skyline Card to storage and pushes signed receipt to customer's configured ticket webhook.
- Observer TTL: Audit Skyline card is kept in hot store for 48h, compact MER retained 30d, full forensic bundle (if collected) moves to archive with retention policy per contract.

Compact log schema examples (plain text for quick ingest):
- Example event (one-line):
  TS=2026-02-25T21:34:12Z EVT=change_request id=cb1f... actor=ops@example.com type=BGP_PEER target=vpc-prod-23 risk=low approver=sofia.p status=approved receipt=mer:cb1f...
- JSON-free format intentionally reduces parsing overhead for simple SIEM forwarding.

Forensic bundle (only for Locked/standard if escalated):
- Full config diffs (git patch), traceroute snapshots, packet-sampled logs (redacted), operator session recording metadata, system traces.
- Archive encrypted with customer-managed KMS key if requested.

UX & Console notes:
- 'Accept & Issue MER' modal: show compact diff + one-click copyable receipt.
- Inline risk explainer: short bullet why risk=low (e.g., "no new egress, change to route priority only, sample telemetry OK").
- Minimal friction for fastpath: keep required fields to a minimum and default safe values.

Metrics / success criteria (pilot):
- Time-to-approval (median) for fastpath under 3 minutes (goal).
- Reduction in stored forensic payloads by 70% (pilot customers).
- Operator-reported false-negative risk misses < 5% in first 3 months.
- Customer acceptance of MER as a compliance artifact (sign-off from at least 2 pilot GRC teams).

Test scenarios (quick list):
- Scenario A: config tweak (route weight) by operator -> fastpath approval -> 48h no forensic bundle collected.
- Scenario B: BGP ASN change by customer -> standard gate -> canary followed by full telemetry -> MER + optional archive.
- Scenario C: emergency rollback after failed migration -> MER stamped with rollback tag + postmortem forensic collection.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Define canonical change_type enum and mapping from existing internal change events. (TODO: PD-9876)
- Formal signature scheme for MER (HSM vs KMS). Need security review. (action: @Maya Rao)
- Retention contract language: what is minimal retention we can promise to customers vs internal needs? Legal input required.
- How to surface MER to customers that are air-gapped? (hint: signed QR card or offline USB escrow).

Appendix: sample MER payload (human-friendly):
-----BEGIN-MER-----
receipt_id: cb1f2b9a-4e3a-11ee-9f34-0242ac120002
receipt_version: 0.3
issuer: redwood-controlplane@redwood.com
subject: acct-8452
change_type: ROUTE_UPDATE
actor: ops-alice@redwood.com
timestamp: 2026-02-25T21:34:12Z
summary_hash: sha256:3a4b...
signature: MIIBIjANBgkqh...
-----END-MER-----

Notes to reviewer:
- This is intentionally pragmatic and operator-facing. Looking for feedback on:
  * MER field set (too verbose? missing anything?)
  * Fastpath gate heuristics and safe defaults
  * Any regulatory gaps we missed (PCI/HIPAA/UK-GDPR telemetry handling)

Slack refs: #private-deploy-ops, thread: sofiapatel/audit-skyline-pilot
Related tickets: JIRA PD-9876 (design), PD-10021 (pilot infra), PD-10100 (security review).

End of doc.
